title: Clean installation of a polynomial-time function
statement: Every polynomial-time computable function $f$ on binary words has a finite Turing machine $M$ and natural numbers $A,d$ such that, for every binary input $x$ and argument word, the computation first halts at a positive time no greater than $A(n+1)^d$, where $n$ is the argument length; at that time its tape words encode $f$ of the argument and its output is empty.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a polynomial-time computable function on binary words
replaced: Every polynomial-time computable string function $f$ has a first-halting clean module that replaces the argument word by $f$ of the argument, emits nothing, and runs within $A(n+1)^d$ steps of the argument length for some constants $A, d$.
